title: Cuda workspace & heap fragmentation — root-cause notes and repros
body:
Quick notes / lab log for memory fragmentation causing intermittent OOMs on prod serving nodes.

Summary (short):
- Symptom: sporadic CUDA OOMs on 48GB A40 nodes under mixed-seq-length traffic, often after several hours even when aggregate live allocations are below device capacity.
- Observed pattern: total free memory reported by cuMemGetInfo decreases in small steps; largest contiguous free block becomes significantly smaller than total free -> classic heap fragmentation.
- Hypothesis: allocator behavior (cudaMalloc/cudaFree + runtime caching) combined with variable-sized temporary allocations (per-request workspaces, attention KV, temp buffers) is leaving many small free holes. When a large workspace allocation is requested (e.g., for long sequence or beam expansion), there isn't a large contiguous block even though sum(free) > request -> OOM.

Important reproduction notes (how we reproduced locally):
- Repro script (rough): loop 1..N do { issue mixed requests: seq_len in {256, 1024, 2048, 8192} with random interleaving; allocate attention KV and temp outputs; free ephemeral buffers }
- On a clean process (fresh driver): memory starts contiguous. After ~10k mixed requests fragmentation ratio grows.
- Commands used to observe memory: 
  - nvidia-smi dmon / nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv -l 1
  - small C test using cuMemGetInfo to sample free/total over time
  - Nsight Systems traces to capture cudaMalloc/cudaFree call sequences and sizes

What we measured (example trace):
- Start: total 48GB, largest free block ≈ 48GB
- After 3 hours: total free ≈ 12.7GB, largest free block ≈ 520MB -> fragmentation_ratio ~ (1 - 520MB/12.7GB) ~ 96%
- Many allocations were 1–50MB ephemeral buffers; periodic large allocations ~4–10GB for long seqs failed.

Allocator interactions to consider (notes):
- cudaMalloc / cudaFree: driver-level semantics can create fragmentation; cudaFree returns blocks to driver heap which may or may not coalesce immediately depending on CUDA runtime version and internal bins.
- cudaMallocAsync (CUDA 11.2+): asynchronous allocator that works with CUDA streams and can reduce latency & fragmentation for ephemeral allocations when used correctly. Requires cudaMemPool support to get full benefits.
- cuMemPool APIs (CUDA 11.3+): allow creating explicit pools (cuMemPoolCreate, cuMemPoolSetAttribute) — recommended for fine-grained control and to avoid kernel-level fragmentation on mixed workloads.
- Library caching allocators (e.g., PyTorch caching allocator): can reduce fragmentation for siloed usage patterns but can also hold onto lots of memory if not tuned for long-lived and short-lived mixed lifetimes.

Root-cause candidates and evidence: 
1) Mixed lifetimes / size distribution -> internal fragmentation
   - Evidence: histogram of allocation sizes shows a very heavy tail: many small allocations (4–64KB and 1–16MB) interleaved with rare huge allocations (>= 1GB).
   - Small blocks freed in many places, large request needs contiguous block -> fail.

2) Allocator not coalescing freed blocks (driver bug / version behavior)
   - Evidence: after freeing, cuMemGetInfo shows total free rising but largest contiguous block remains small; repeating malloc/free orders doesn't create coalesced large block. Behaviour changed between driver versions (we saw slightly better coalesce on 525.x vs 515.x).

3) Per-engine workspace sizing mismatch (TensorRT or custom kernels)
   - Some engines request a workspace via cudaMalloc when preparing scratch for kernels. If workspace sizing sometimes spikes beyond pool bin sizing, allocator must split bigger chunk which may not exist contiguous.
   - Evidence: when we forced maximum workspace to be capped (pre-allocated a single large workspace per-device and reused), OOMs drop dramatically.

4) Cross-thread/stream allocation ordering causing fragmentation
   - Asynchronous alloc/free across streams can delay actual free until stream completes; ordering means holes are not available when another stream attempts large alloc.
   - Evidence: enabling cudaDeviceSynchronize periodically reduced OOM frequency (cheap but impacts latency).

Experiments run and results (short log):
- Baseline: no special allocator changes -> OOM after ~2–4 hours under mixed realtime traffic.
- Turned on cudaMallocAsync for ephemeral allocs -> fragmentation growth slope reduced, OOMs delayed/avoided in 60% of runs.
- Created single device mempool and pre-reserved 32GB workspace region, rewired long-lived allocations to sub-allocate from this region -> OOMs eliminated in 90% of runs, but observed increased tail latency when using large pre-allocated block due to contention.
- Forced power-of-two arena allocator in our runtime (64KB min bin) -> small improvement, but large allocations still failed if total highest free block fragmented.

Practical mitigations (recommendations to try, ranked):
1) Short-term (low risk)
   - Pre-allocate a large reusable workspace per device (configurable, e.g., reserve 28–36GB on 48GB cards) and route large workspace requests to sub-allocations within it. This guarantees a contiguous region for big allocations.
   - Add a per-request check: if requested workspace > largest_free_block (from cuMemGetInfo), try to compact or fail early with soft-fallback to smaller model.

2) Medium-term (requires code changes)
   - Switch ephemeral allocations to cudaMallocAsync + mempool to reduce fragmentation from many small transient buffers. Requires CUDA 11.2+ and stream-aligned alloc/free semantics.
   - Introduce separate allocators/pools for long-lived structures (KV caches, model weights) and for ephemeral scratch. Avoid mixing lifetimes in same pool.

3) Long-term / runtime-level improvements
   - Implement an arena allocator inside the runtime with size-class bins and chunk coalescing on free; prefer power-of-two binning to limit fragmentation.
   - Integrate CUDA mempool APIs for deterministic pooling and set attributes for release thresholds.

Instrumentation we should add (dev tasks):
- Allocation trace: lightweight logging of allocation sizes + timestamps + stream/owner id (ring-buffer, sample 1:1000) to reproduce allocation patterns without full tracing overhead.
- Periodically sample cuMemGetInfo and largest-free-block estimate (we implemented small native helper that calls cuMemGetInfo + tries to malloc largest candidate sizes to find largest contiguous block; expensive but useful for debugging mode).
- Add histogram dashboards (per-instance): alloc size, free frequency, avg lifetime, fragmentation ratio = 1 - (largest_block / total_free).
- Integrate Nsight Systems profiles for failing runs and store samples with request ids.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is there an upstream CUDA driver version where coalescing behavior is significantly improved? We saw differences between 515.x and 525.x but need broader matrix across 510–540.
- Interaction with cuBLAS/cuDNN workspace allocations: they sometimes internally request temporary memory; do they use mempool APIs or raw cudaMalloc? Need to audit versions.
- Does enabling MPS (multi-process service) change fragmentation behavior for our workload (we run multiple processes per GPU for isolation)?
- Side-effect risk: large pre-allocated workspace reduces fragmentation but reduces scheduling flexibility for multi-tenant. Need tuning per-customer.

Quick checklist for next 2 sprints: 
- [ ] Add sampled allocation trace hook to runtime (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Prototype cudaMallocAsync path for ephemeral buffers (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Build configurable per-device pre-allocated workspace and integration test (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Run driver matrix tests (515/520/525/535) with synthetic mixed-seq load and log fragmentation metrics (owner: Samir)

Notes to self: keep this doc informal; move polished recommendations to Confluence after we have the driver matrix and allocator trace data.

References & quick links: 
- CUDA mempool docs: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDA__MEMPOOL.html
- cudaMallocAsync overview: https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/using-cudamallocasync/
- Nsight Systems: capture cudaMalloc/cudaFree timeline and stream interactions
- GH#redwood/runtime#4521 (prototype mempool + workspace manager)

Last experimental snapshot: 
- commit: prototype/allocator-mempool@c3f2b6 (local branch)
- test harness: tools/mem-frag-test.py (random-mix-seq)
- outcome: with 32GB pre-reserve + cudaMallocAsync enabled for ephemeral allocs: no OOM for 24h stability run on 48GB A40 box (synthetic mixed traffic).

Unresolved: decide default reserve size heuristics (fraction of device or absolute) for different SKUs (A30/A40/H100). Run cost tradeoff analysis for Dedicated capacity customers.
